thread.title: US Economic Data Remains Healthy But Some Recent Measures Reflect A Slowing

author: Nasdaq
title: US Economic Data Remains Healthy But Some Recent Measures Reflect A Slowing
text:
Shutterstock photo Friday, November 2, 2018, 12:07 PM, EST NASDAQ Composite -1.29% Dow -0.55% S&P 500 -0.75% Russell 2000 -0.36% NASDAQ Advancers: 1183 Decliners: 1305 Movers Apple -6.5% ArcBest +14.5% Redfin -6.6% Starbucks +9.7% Synchrony -8.2% Nonfarm Payrolls beat with 250k new positions added Private Payrolls +246k; Manufacturing +32k National Unemployment Rate held steady at 3.7% Ave hourly Earnings met expectations +0.2% Labor Participation Rate increased by 0.2% to 62.9% Factory Orders (Sept) beat with a 0.7% gain, and August was revised higher Steve's Commentary
The global rally continues across Asia and Europe, but the US markets gave back early gains and are somewhat lower. Yesterday Trump stoked optimism on a potential trade agreement with China and went so far as to ask his staff to begin drafting the terms. Whether his comments have substance or are simply a pre-election gimmick is anyone's guess, but it boosted sentiment nevertheless. China's Shanghai Composite gained 2.7% over night and that was its 4th consecutive gain, the first time that's happened since February.
Here at home the major indices opened modestly higher but rolled into the red after the first hour. No specific reason for the pull-back other than profit-taking after three strong sessions, and White House officials stress that at best an agreement with China won't occur until the G-20 Meeting at the end of the month.
The Dow and SPX are fractionally lower but the Nasdaq Composite is off the most on pressure from tech stocks, and the action has been a little choppy. The R2K is down the least if the major indexes, which is impressive in itself after surging over 2% just yesterday.
Results from Starbucks and Newell Brands lift the Consumer Discretionary (+0.2%) to the top of the sector rankings. Technology however, is down 2% following results from Apple. The Energy space is holding a slight 0.1% gain despite crude oil trading lower for a 5th day now down about 17% since October 3rd.
With the markets higher for the week it is not surprising that money flows are favorable. Equity ETFs saw modest inflows of $2.9 billion directed toward large cap and broad market funds, but sector based funds saw outflows of $818 million. Also freeing up capital are corporate share buybacks, which are coming back online as earnings related blackouts roll off.
US economic data remains healthy although some recent measures reflect a slowing. That is not the case on the employment front; Nonfarm payrolls in October exceeded the +200k estimate with a +250k print, and private and manufacturing payrolls also exceeded expectations. Interestingly manufacturing payrolls came in at +32k, double expectations and the highest since December, yet yesterday's ISM Manufacturing number missed and hit a six-month low.
Wage growth has been lacking in recent years but Average Hourly Wages in October rose to 3.1% y/y from 2.8% last month, and that is the first time since 2009 that wage growth exceeded 3%. The good news on the employment front gets us another notch closer to a rate hike in December, which is not necessarily good news to some. Yields are higher this morning with the 10-year treasury at 3.17%, however the dollar index is off 0.1%.
Next week the midterm election go down in the history books, but unfortunately the 2020 election cycle ramps up. It is the last of the earnings deluge with 892 reports expected. There is a FOMC meeting but no rate hike is expected, and sanctions on Iranian oil go into effect but eight countries are exempted including Japan and South Korea. As for the economic calendar, look for ISM Non-Manufacturing, and PPI & CPI inflation measures. Also next week Charlie Brown takes the reigns with the updates from the MID.

Brian's Technical Take
Is good news good?
US employers added 250,000 jobs in October with rages rising the most since 2009, +3.1% YoY. Accordingly rates and the dollar are higher as the strong payroll number is inflationary while the spike in new hires suggests the current economic cycle may not be as late as many have feared. Today the higher yielding defensive sectors - REITs , utilities, and staples - are in the red, along with technology which is being weighed down by AAPL. Leading to the upside is the consumer discretionary sector, +1.7% at its intraday highs, which fits nicely with the accelerating wages script.
It will be interesting to see if the positive reaction can hold up as we know with stocks, sometimes good news is bad. Not long ago in the first week of February, strong wage data, +2.8% YoY, led to concerns of an increasingly hawkish Fed and double digit declines in all of the equity indices in two weeks' time.
Most global indices peaked at this time as well. Today's highs in the SPX measures 153 points that it has rebounded off of the October lows made just four days ago on Monday. This comes within 0.5% of the 50% Fibonacci Retracement of the entire October selloff. The low hanging fruit has been picked and now is the time for bulls to show what they are made of.
Back to the discretionary index, after leading all sectors to the downside in October with a monthly decline of 11.3%, it is currently +4.7% this week for its best weekly gain since January 2013. However it too has a big test right here and now at the 860 - 870 zone where a cluster of technical resistance resides representing: (i) the 200-day moving average (yellow line), now 862, (ii) the January pivot high, 870, and (iii) the underbelly of the rising trend line from the 2016 lows, which had proven to be a critical support line over the prior 30+ months ending October given the high number of times it has been tested and held firm.
Prior support often turns to resistance and all three factors combined make this an obvious zone to expect overhead supply to kick in. The easy ground has been captured by the bulls. Now the real battle begins.
